prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas to Try to Beat the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that will beat the S&P 500 over a single year. In a typical year, about 60–65% of professional large-cap fund managers fail to beat it, and over 15 years roughly 90% do. Treat the list below as a starting point for your own research, not a prediction.

**My information may be out of date.** My knowledge runs to about May 2026, and I can't see live prices. Valuations and news may have changed a lot since then, so check current prices and recent earnings before buying anything.

## The ideas

| # | Company (Ticker) | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all leading-edge AI chips. It isn't in the S&P 500, so owning it is a real bet away from the index. | China/Taiwan tensions |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Designs custom AI chips for hyperscalers (large cloud providers) and sells AI networking gear. | High valuation; depends on a few big customers |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Cheaper than most mega-cap tech peers, with a growing cloud business, its own AI chips, and Waymo (self-driving cars). | AI disrupting search; antitrust cases |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS growth, a high-margin ad business and improving retail margins. | Heavy AI spending weighing on cash flow |
| 5 | **Micron (MU)** | Strong demand for the high-speed memory that AI chips need. | Memory is cyclical, and it may already be near a peak |
| 6 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Large order backlog for gas turbines and grid equipment to power data centers. | Priced for strong execution |
| 7 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in obesity and diabetes drugs, including a pill version in the pipeline. | Drug pricing pressure; competition |
| 8 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-in-class bank that benefits from dealmaking, trading and lighter regulation. | A credit downturn or recession |
| 9 | **CrowdStrike (CRWD)** | Cybersecurity spending holds up well even when budgets tighten. | Expensive; worries about AI disrupting software |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Holds a large cash pile and tends to beat the index when markets fall. | Likely to lag in a strong bull market |

## How to think about this list

- **It leans heavily on AI.** About six of the ten names depend on AI spending continuing. If that trend cools, this portfolio will probably do worse than the S&P 500, not better.
- **Beating the index requires being different from it.** Overlap is a problem: Alphabet, Amazon and Broadcom are already among the S&P 500's largest holdings. Names like TSM, Micron and GE Vernova are what actually make this portfolio differ from the index.
- **A common middle path:** keep most of your money (say 70–80%) in a low-cost S&P 500 fund. Use the remaining 20–30% for picks like these. You get a chance to outperform without risking falling far behind.
- **Size positions sensibly.** Put no more than about 5–10% of your portfolio in any one stock. Decide in advance what would make you sell each one.
- **One year is a short window.** Short-term results are mostly luck. Taxes and trading costs also cut into any gains.

If you tell me your total amount, your risk tolerance, whether the money is in a taxable or retirement account, and what you already own, I can tailor the list. This is general information, not personalized financial advice. For a large amount, a fee-only financial advisor is worth considering.
